subject: imputation functions don't work for me

messages.author: 8c88e75d9eb66be4
messages.subject: imputation functions don't work for me
parts:
Hello,

I have processed my data using the following parameters but it seems that the imputation built-in functions don't work well. First, the quantification results are exactly identical. Second, there are some missing values (NAs) in the final table.  Could you please help me with this?

Best,
Amir


df.MSstats.proc.Imputed <- dataProcess(raw = df.annot.MSstats, logTrans=2, normalization="equalizeMedians", nameStandards=NULL,
                                       remove_uninformative_feature_outlier = FALSE, featureSubset = 'top3', summaryMethod = 'TMP',
                                       censoredInt = 'NA', MBimpute = TRUE)

df.MSstats.proc.NAs <- dataProcess(raw = df.annot.MSstats, logTrans=2, normalization="equalizeMedians", nameStandards=NULL,
                                   remove_uninformative_feature_outlier = FALSE, featureSubset = 'top3', summaryMethod = 'TMP',
                                   censoredInt = NULL, MBimpute = FALSE)

df.MSstats.proc.Imputed.quant <- quantification(data = df.MSstats.proc.Imputed, type = 'Sample', format = 'matrix')
df.MSstats.proc.NAs.quant <- quantification(data = df.MSstats.proc.NAs, type = 'Sample', format = 'matrix')

messages.author: 8c88e75d9eb66be4
messages.subject: Re: imputation functions don't work for me
parts:
An update on this issue.

It seems that it only imputes for "0" values regardless of the censoredInt = 'NA' option. NAs remained missing values even after the imputation but '0's would have been changed to the imputated one. Any comment?

Best,
Amir
